result_text:
The booking grid now follows local opening hours on clock-change days. The cause was `localTimeToUtc` in `src/lib/slots.ts`, which read the timezone offset at UTC midnight of the date instead of at the requested local time. On 28 March 2027 that gave 11:00 for a 10:00 Berlin opening, and on 31 October it gave 09:00.

The fix reads the offset at the target wall time and does a second pass in case the first guess falls on the other side of a transition. Every caller goes through this function, so the slots route, booking availability, and the admin day view are all covered.

I added regression tests to `src/lib/slots.test.ts`: Berlin spring-forward and fall-back, plus a New York spring-forward case. Unit tests pass (16/16) and ESLint is clean on both files. I didn't run the integration tests or the dev server, since Postgres and Redis aren't available here. `tsc --noEmit` reports one error in `src/app/layout.tsx`, which I didn't touch and which comes from generated Next.js types.

Changes are uncommitted in the working tree.
